description: the gateway routing config exists as a reviewed artifact — WHICH model serves WHICH traffic class is version-controlled, not hidden in code
command: [ -f platform/gateway/routing.yaml ] && yq -e '.routes.support.model' platform/gateway/routing.yaml >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: the provider+pricing map exists — model tiers resolve to a price and a provider latency profile the four-dials view reads
command: [ -f platform/gateway/providers.yaml ] && yq -e '.models.deep.price_per_1m_usd' platform/gateway/providers.yaml >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: the routing-change review gate exists and is executable — a route change is priced as a cost + latency decision, not read as a config typo
REGRESSION: gateway-diff flags the support route moving from fast to deep — the one-line flip the whole incident is about
command: scripts/gateway-diff.sh --field changed | jq -e '.[] | select(.route=="support") | select(.from=="fast" and .to=="deep")' >/dev/null && echo pass || echo fail

description: REGRESSION: with support on a costlier AND slower tier, the diff verdict is 'review-required' — the change gate refuses to wave it through
command: [ "$(scripts/gateway-diff.sh --field verdict)" = review-required ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: COST DIAL: the diff attaches a per-day support-workload cost delta to the route flip — the number has an address, not just a total (M11 pattern carried forward)
the four-dials reader exists and is executable — latency, token cost, rate limits, and quality read together for a route
LATENCY DIAL: on the regressed route the support p95 reads 9500ms — the deep tier's provider latency, far past a support SLO
command: [ "$(scripts/llm-dials.sh dials support --field latency_p95)" = 9500 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: RATE-LIMIT DIAL: routing 300k tpm at a provider whose deep-tier ceiling is 120k yields NEGATIVE tpm headroom — the flip silently over-committed the provider limit
command: [ "$(scripts/llm-dials.sh dials support --field tpm_headroom | cut -d. -f1)" -lt 0 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: PROVIDER vs APPLICATION: splitting the regressed trace shows provider time dominant — the latency is the model, not our code, so the fix is the route not the app
command: [ "$(scripts/llm-dials.sh split fixtures/gateway/traces/support-regressed.json --field dominant)" = provider ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: PROVIDER vs APPLICATION: application-span time is ~unchanged between baseline and regressed traces (<=400ms both) — falsifies 'our code got slower'
command: B=$(scripts/llm-dials.sh split fixtures/gateway/traces/support-baseline.json --field application_ms); R=$(scripts/llm-dials.sh split fixtures/gateway/traces/support-regressed.json --field application_ms); [ "$B" -le 400 ] && [ "$R" -le 400 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: PROMPT IN GIT: the support-summarize prompt is a version-controlled artifact, reviewed like code — not a string buried in application source
command: [ -f platform/gateway/prompts/support-summarize.txt ] && grep -q 'order ID' platform/gateway/prompts/support-summarize.txt && echo pass || echo fail

description: the Promptfoo-style regression gate exists and is executable — the quality dial made into a CI check
QUALITY GATE: the good output set passes every required assertion — verdict pass, exit 0
QUALITY GATE: the regressed set (invented refund, dropped order ID, guaranteed date) fails required assertions — verdict fail, so CI would block the change
command: if scripts/promptfoo-gate.sh evals/promptfoo/support-summarize.yaml --set regressed --field verdict >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo passed; else echo blocked; fi

description: YOUR DIAGNOSIS: agentops/m16-diagnosis.md names the regressed route, the correct model tier, and the cost or latency evidence — the durable output of this module, since the revert itself is undone at teardown
command: D=agentops/m16-diagnosis.md; [ -f $D ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; ok=1; grep -qi 'support' $D || ok=0; grep -qi 'fast' $D || ok=0; grep -Eqi 'cost|latency|rpm|tpm|p95' $D || ok=0; [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] && echo recorded || echo incomplete
